dataSetInformation.common:generalComment: The dataset has been developed on the basis of the operation of the average US PWR with average burnup of 37.5 MWd-th/kg heavy metal (reload 2006) assumed representative for the lifetime of the modelled plant. The average burnup corresponds to an average enrichment of 3.8% U235 for fuel elements, all using fresh uranium because reprocessing is not permitted in the USA. The utilisation factor for the infrastructure is the inverse of the total net electricity delivered in 40 years lifetime, calculated assuming an average Load Factor = 85% (2003-2006 LF was 90.9% but lifetime LF up to September 2006 was 77.8%). Material requirements have been extrapolated from the Swiss PWR by the ratio of the capacity factors. The transport requirements for materials (e.g. chemicals) are calculated using ecoinvent standard distances for Europe. Radioactive emission species to air and water are taken from US data of all individual PWR units and represent the average in the time period 2000-2005. The radioactive waste streams are modelled along the Swiss datasets, for this part of the US chain has not been explicitly assessed for ecoinvent v2.0; UUID: bb60a284-9cda-332e-8e2e-e0d3a26e85bf

locationOfOperationSupplyOrProduction.descriptionOfRestrictions: US data for PWRs on radioactive emissions, efficiency, load factor, burnup, enrichment. Swiss data of one specific PWR for other parameters, adapted.

technology.technologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse:
Standard technology for commercial operation.

# Included processes
The module includes fuel elements, chemicals, and diesel requirements as well as the relevant transport requirements. Water use (fresh from sea and decarbonized) for cooling is included. Considered radioactive waste streams are: spent fuel to conditioning (no reprocessing); operational low active waste for conditioning in the intermediate repository; and, contaminated waste from dismantling. Non-radioactive wastes are accounted for.
